admission.justification: The reviewed default widths, independent tree/chat class keys, shared handle setters and shell/overlay placement must agree. Adjacent hidden-panel and frame-lifetime obligations cannot prevent a resize overwriting another class/rail or an overlay reverting to an unrelated width. Tree/keyboard/pointer proof limits are explicitly retained.

applicability: The review page tree and task-chat rail numeric widths and their existing shared resize handles, in wide/narrow viewport classes and grid/overlay/narrow chat placement.
conditions: Above1600px the default tree/chat widths are340px/500px with14px gutter; at-or-below1600px defaults are292px/420px with12px gutter. A finite saved numeric value for that rail/class replaces its default.

Tree and chat store separate wide/narrow numeric values under cockpit.review.tree-w.{wide,narrow} and cockpit.review.chat-w.{wide,narrow}; these do not reuse cockpit.rail-left-w or cockpit.rail-right-w.

The class-specific width setter is passed to the named shared RailResizeHandle. Requested pointer and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight resizing is rounded and bounded220..560px; arrow changes are24px mirrored by side. The stored read itself is not newly clamped.

Below1440px the open chat uses its active-class width in absolute overlay placement, and at40rem or narrower uses that width with a viewport max-width in fixed placement. Placement does not allocate another width key or reset the chosen class value.

At40rem and narrower the shared resize handle is absent and the review grid stacks. A hidden tree has a zero layout track without overwriting its class value; a closed or overlying chat has a zero shell grid track and retains the active gutter.
exclusions: The separate shared-control policy owns hidden-side width release, reachable overlay controls and grid-track visibility; this record adds the numeric class/preference/resize contract rather than replacing RP16.
INV-Z385RTQS owns Changes only/Full context preference and split/unified switching by reading content width; this record does not promise exact measured reading-column widths or diff geometry.
Operations numeric rail preferences, Knowledge/File Viewer/notes panel autosave sizes, host-native sidebar widths, visibility open-state persistence and frame continuity.
Shared resize bounds apply to requested handle changes; finite persisted values are not claimed to be range-clamped on read. Numeric preference storage failure recovery is outside this width policy.

evidence: MIK-R89@v2 rules1 (Columns/Rails),11 (Widths) and accepted W26 width classes/gutters; canonical L89 task and its approved packet govern, with immutable Worker entries at zero-based ordinals 3,31,107,123,152. Producer dispositions remain verbatim in the companion helper review; this is a Curator supplemental projection, not replacement producer data.

statement: The review tree and chat keep separate resizable widths per viewport class; their saved class widths survive chat placement changes between grid and overlays.
